---
title: "Poisson regression verification record"
---

The [executed comparison](../notebooks/poisson-verification.qmd) fits identical
observations in base R `glm()`, statsmodels `GLM`, and PHP `fit_poisson_matrix()`.
The [saved report](poisson-results.json) records versions, complete outputs,
maximum differences from R, warnings and retained-row metadata.

## Reference cases and conventions

Six saved R fixtures cover the simulated clinic sample, a single predictor,
multiple predictors, no intercept, intercept only, correlated full-rank columns
and sparse counts (the main sample is the multiple-predictor case).
The three-way comparison adds listwise deletion of two rows. All coefficients,
covariance entries, standard errors, normal z tests and p-values, Wald confidence
limits, full fitted mean counts and response residuals, likelihood, deviance,
null deviance, AIC and residual df are checked. Numerical tolerance is
1e-9 + 1e-7 × abs(reference); sample accounting is exact.

R uses `confint.default(fit)`, not profile-likelihood `confint(fit)`.
Its fitting tolerance is 1e-16 to make covariance evaluated at the preceding
IRLS iterate negligible. Iteration counts can differ across implementations;
they are not a reference equality requirement. Without a ones column the null
baseline is mean one; the Python runner computes this convention explicitly.

## Failure and integration checks

Rust/PHP tests reject insufficient observations, invalid shapes, nonfinite or
negative/fractional outcomes, all-zero samples, dependent columns, and selected boundary designs. They check scaled predictor units, zero-count and near-fit deviance arithmetic, iteration exhaustion, missing-row warnings and alignment.
OLS integration tests also run after changes to the shared PHP conversion code.
No exhaustive finite-MLE existence test is supplied. Count overdispersion and
sparse samples can invalidate conventional Wald inference. Offsets and exposure
arguments are outside the first implementation. Linux and PHP-FPM deployment have not been exercised by these reports.

## Reproduce

From the repository root with matching PHP development tools:

```sh
export PHP=/opt/homebrew/bin/php
export PHP_CONFIG=/opt/homebrew/bin/php-config
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo build -p phit --locked
php -n -d "extension=$PWD/target/debug/libphit.dylib" tests/poisson.php
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_poisson.py
QUARTO_PYTHON="$PWD/.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python" quarto render docs/notebooks/poisson-verification.qmd
```

Use `.so` on Linux. R fixture regeneration is an explicit development step:
`Rscript tests/generate-probit-poisson-fixtures.R`. Ordinary Rust/PHP tests use saved
fixtures without R or Python. See [development](../development.qmd) for setup and
[large-sample benchmarks](../benchmarks/poisson.qmd) for additional evidence.
